main_text.p: non tamen hinc sequitur, cum pœnas nostris peccatis debitas non persolvisse, nec ideo satisfecisse.

Hæc enim temporaria Passio & Mors Christi, si non præponderat, certe æquivalet æternis nostris suppliciis. Tanta quippe est dignitas passionis & mortis Christi, ut sit pretium sufficiens pro redemptione generis humani. Idque ex his concurrentibus in Christo causis.

Causa sa- tisfactoria. 1. Spontanea obedientia.PRIMA causa est spontanea obedientia filii ad mortem usque crucis. Philip. 2. Satisfactoria enim non fuisset Christi passio, nisi fuisset voluntaria. Hinc Apostolus Roman. 5. v. 19. ait: Sicut per inobedientiam unius peccatores constituti sunt multi: ita per unius obedientiam justi constituuntur multi. Loquitur autem, ut Theophylactus dicit, de obedientia mortis CHRISTI, per quam obedi-entiam morte contrita, ex mortis su-mus erepti condemnatione.
2. Summa innocentia.Secunda causa, quod Christus non tantum sponte sua se obtulerit, ad nos redimendum, adeoque ejus humiliatio & mort

page.notes: Running head and page number read from a small, worn print; "148" and the end of the running head are uncertain. The right-edge marks are the neighbouring page and were left out. The word after "ex mortis" (su-mus) is hyphenated at the line end and is doubtful. The page ends mid-word ("& mort"), as printed.
